components.notes:
We’ve had handstand push-ups in the program for the past two cycles and today is a little benchmark session. While the program has mostly focused on the foundations of the skill as well as strength-building specific to the movement, today we will dip our toes into strength endurance.
Advanced athletes should create a smart strategy to attack this and see how quickly they can work through this volume of reps.
Athletes who can perform the skill as prescribed (no Abmats) but may not have the “density” to get to 50 reps can opt to chip away and see how far they get in the timecap.
Athletes who are still building strength for the full skill should choose a challenging scaling option below to complete your version of 50 reps for time:
A. Strict HSPU: Scaled ROM to 1-3 Spongey Dots or 1 AbMat
B. Box Piked HSPU: Perform the variation you used two weeks ago (Single Leg, Feet on Box, or Knees on Box)
C. Strict DB Press: Use same weight as two weeks ago

components.details:
20 Rounds for Time
10 Ball Slams
100′ Sled Sprint
components.notes:
In teams of four athletes, with one person working at a time, take turns on full rounds of the couplet until the team has finished 20 rounds, 5 for each person.
Use light weights today. Many athletes will get the most effective workout today by using an empty sled. Practice cycling your ball slams efficiently and then sprint!

Today’s workout is simple. Push harder than you want to on the run and find a smooth cadence on the sit-ups.

components.notes:
“Hope” has the same format as Fight Gone Bad. In this workout you move from each of five stations after a minute. This is a five-minute round from which a one-minute break is allowed before repeating. The clock does not reset or stop between exercises. On call of “rotate,” the athletes move to the next station. One point is given for each rep.
Add your points and post them to BTWB.
This benchmark workout features three bodyweight calisthentic movements and two barbell movements with very light weight. Expect it to burn 🔥 Scale barbell load and box height as needed so you can move with good mechanics throughout the workout.
CFSBK’s own Toni Smith has a logged score of 262 reps for this on BTWB!
Create a strategy to maximize your score while finding a pace that allows you to work at relatively high intensity for all three rounds. Scale barbell loading such that you could cycle 10+ reps at a time if desired.
Pull-Up Scaling
A. Chin Over Bar Pull-up (kipping or strict)
B. Foot Assisted Pull-up

components.details: Turkish Get-Up
components.notes:
Accumulate a total of at least 12 quality reps on each side today, more if time allows. Trade arms as desired. Keep your eyes on the weight you’re using and use your core to stabilize your body throughout each rep. Take a beat to pause in each phase of the movement to create clear landmarks for yourself with this multi-part exercise.
Beginners: Use light to moderate loads throughout.
Int/Adv: Once you’ve established clear mechanics and consistency at light weights, build in load to something challenging for the day.

components.details:
Front Squat
Work up to a heavy single in 22 minutes.
components.notes:
Today we are aiming to build confidence under heavy load, dial in bracing, and assess our current strength without maxing out recklessly. Heavy Single = A strong, challenging lift with good form. Not necessarily a lifetime PR. Stop before technique breaks down.
Start with 3-5 warm up sets sets of 3–5 reps. Once you’re at a challenging weight, drop to singles and aim for another 3-5 working sets. For example:
– – – Warm-Up Sets – – –
45 x 5
95 x 5
125 x 4
150 x 3
– – – Work Sets – – –
165 x 1
175 x 1
180 x 1
185 x 1
Remember: “Heavy” today depends on how you’re feeling. Quality movement > chasing numbers.

components.details:

A. 20 Wall Ball Shots
B. 15/12 Calories Row
C. 5 Sandbag Cleans
components.notes:
Stimulus: This is a grindy, sustainable EMOM. Work should take ~40–45 seconds per station, leaving a little recovery and transition time before the next minute.
Wall Ball: It’s a good day to get out of your comfort zone here! Increase the weight of your ball or/and the height of your target to test your accuracy, without compromising mechanics.
Row: Target a consistent pace (not a sprint). Think “strong pulls, steady recovery.”
Sandbag Cleans: Lap the bag first, then hug it and drive tall. Use your hips, not your arms, and keep the bag close. Stay braced, breathe between reps, and aim for smooth sets of 5.

components.details:

400m Run
Max Strict Pull-ups
components.notes:
In this 20-minute AMRAP you’ll run 400 meters, then go straight into a max set of strict pull-ups. Remember, strict doesn’t mean slow, stay tight (hollow shape); drive your elbows down, and pull your chin quickly over the bar. Use the run as your recovery so you can keep hitting quality pull-ups each round. Most athletes should aim for five to six total rounds.
Scaling:
If you have strict pull-ups but are unable to perform at least 5 reps, begin each set with a max set of strict pull-ups, then stay on the bar for a max set of kipping pull-ups. If you do not yet have strict pull-ups, perform a moderately challenging version of banded strict pull-ups or ring rows.
In case of injury or limitation, perform 800/1,000 meters on a bike or 400/500 meters on a rower. For the strict pull-ups, if hanging is not an option for you, you can perform dumbbell bent-over rows.
Scaling option A:
400m Run
Max-rep strict pull-ups + kipping pull-ups
Scaling option B:
400m Run
Max-rep banded strict pull-ups

components.notes:
After 1-2 lighter warm up sets on the barbell, perform the two movements as a superset, resting about 60-90 sec between each.
Complete all the lunges on one side before changing to the other side.
In this first week of the cycle, focus on quality reps with as close to perfect mechanics as you can achieve and holding the tempo for the RDLs. Use a regular grip or hook grip; no switch grip today.

components.details:
“Half Flight Simulator”
For Time
10-20-30-40-50-40-30-20-10
Unbroken Double Unders
Time Cap: 10 min
components.notes:
With a running clock, perform 10 unbroken Double-Unders. Stop. Perform 20 unbroken Double-Unders. Stop. Perform 30 Double-Unders, etc. Continue with this pattern, increasing by 10 until the set of 50 unbroken Double-Unders, then back down to 10.
Each set must be unbroken. The rope must stop moving before starting the next set. Rest as needed between sets. A failed Double-Under (either because the rope stops or because the rope passes under the feet only once) counts as a broken set. If a set is broken, start again from the beginning of that set.
Today’s workout involves 250 total repetitions. Choose a scaling option below that challenges your skill while allowing you to finish in under 8 minutes. Advanced athletes should target completing this under 4 minutes.
A. 5-10-15-20-25-20-15-10-5 (125 reps)
B. Complete 10 Sets of 10 Unbroken Reps for Time (100 reps)
C. Accumulate 50 total Double Unders or Attempts (count your misses as well as your makes)
D. 15-30-45-60-75-60-45-30-15 Unbroken Single Unders

components.details:

4 x 5 @ 70% or RPE 6-7
components.notes:
Our goal here is to accumulate some volume with technically sound, crisp reps and establish a baseline of good mechanics with the rack position, vertical dip, and leg drive.
Today, reset at the rack position for each rep, rather than cycling or linking the reps together through the dip.
If you have a recent or well-established 1 rep max, use ~70% of that for your work sets. If not, go by rate of perceived exertion and work in the realm of 6-7 for how you’re feeling today.
Either way, this will be moderate load and you should have multiple good reps in the tank left on each set. Ideally we get 4 working sets at the same weight, but a little wiggle room is fine here for today.

A. 7-5-3

components.notes:

March: Use two heavy KBs that challenge your grip. Stand tall and stay balanced as you march steadily in place. If you are not coming to class tomorrow and want to challenge your upper back strength instead, perform a dual KB front rack march.
Sit-ups: Each rep starts with the fingertips touching the floor overhead and finishes with fingertips touching the toes. If needed, scale to touch as far forward as your mobility allows. Athletes with strict or kipping toes to bar can elect to do that movement today (but not recommended if you came to class yesterday).

4×5 @ 65%-70%
components.notes:
Our goal today is to accumulate some volume with technically sound, crisp reps and establish a baseline of good mechanics with the front rack position, vertical torso, and speed out of the hole.
If you were here for the heavy single, use about 65% up to 70% of your best rep. If you did not come last Monday, work at a load that feels like RPE 5 to 6.
Either way, this will be moderate load and you should have multiple good reps in the tank left on each set.

components.details:
3 Rounds for Time
16 Alternating DB Hang Power Snatches
30 Air Squats
12 Box Jump Overs (24/20″)
Intent: 6-10min
components.notes:
The workout is designed to be short and punchy. Push the pace but don’t blow up in Round 1. Find a sustainable speed in the air squats and then attack the snatches and box jumps. Aim to keep each round under 3 minutes to hit the intended stimulus.
DB: Choose a weight you can cycle confidently and complete unbroken or in two quick sets max.
Move smoothly through the air squats, don’t rush and lose depth, but keep a steady rhythm.
The box jump overs are where heart rate will spike, so stay efficient with footwork and step down if needed to keep moving safely. Scale height of the box as low as needed today!

components.details: Handstand kick ups and Holds
components.notes:
Today is all about building confidence and control upside down. Use the time to practice smooth kick-ups and strong, active handstand holds. Keep the focus on technique and body position.
When kicking up, start small and controlled, then build height as you feel more confident. Think about stacking your hips over your shoulders and pressing the floor away with strong, active arms. Don’t rush, find balance with tight legs and a strong core.
For the handstand holds, aim for short sets of 10–20 seconds where you can stay in a good hollow body position. Quality holds will help you build strength and balance faster than maxing out until you fall.
Practice safe bail-outs. If you feel yourself tipping over, turn your body into a cartwheel rather than crashing down.

components.details:
A1. Barbell Good Mornings, 4×6-8
A2. Rear Foot Elevated Split Squats, 4×6-8ea
components.notes:
After 1-2 warm up sets with the barbell, perform the two movements as a superset, resting about 60-90 sec between each.
Use a slower-down, faster-up tempo on both exercises.
Good Mornings: Maintain a braced, rigid trunk and perform the movement by flexing and extending at the hips. Focus your attention on stretching and loading into the glutes and hamstrings on the descent of each rep.
Split Squats: Hold 1 or 2 DB’s suitcase style. If balance is a challenge for you, grab a pvc pipe to hold/push into the ground to assist you. Complete all reps on one side before changing to the other side.

components.details:
For Time
10 Power Cleans @ 155/105#
400m Run
20 Power Cleans
800m Run
components.notes:
Intent: 8-13 min
Load is on the heavier side of moderate, in the realm of 60-70%. Scale to a weight you are comfortable completing quick singles with and could cycle a few unbroken reps if required.
If your 800m / half mile run pace is greater than 5 minutes, consider scaling one or both runs back slightly:
A. 270m (4th Ave and back) / 680m (full lap + 3rd Ave and back)
B. 200m (mural and back) / 550m (full lap)

130m Run + 400m Bike / 270m Run + 800m Bike

components.details:

5 sets x 3 reps @ 75%-80% or RPE 7
components.notes:
This is our second and final week with push press before we progress to the push jerk. Dial in your rack position, dip, and leg drive today — all of that will carry over to the rest of the cycle!
If you have a recent or well-established 1 rep max, use ~75-80% of that for your work sets. If not, work at about RPE 7 for how you feel today.
Either way, this should be heavier than last week, and you should still have a couple reps in the tank on each set.

components.details:

10 ea Single Arm DB Chainsaw Row
40 sec Dual KB Front Rack March
5-10 Strict Toes to Bar @ 2 sec down tempo
1:00 Bike @ recovery pace
components.notes:
Start with moderate loads for the first two movements and work up in weight as long as you are able to maintain consistent mechanics.
Toes to Bar: Hold the tempo! Control throughout. No swing, no kip. Minimize lat pushdown in this variation. Scale the movement to Incline Strict TTB i if needed so you can work on active compression through the abs and hip flexors to bring the legs to the torso.

components.details:
A. Front Squat, 4×5 @ 65-70%
B. Rear Foot Elevated Split Squat, 4 x 6-8

components.notes:
Tomorrow we have pull-ups and thrusters.
You may superset your main lift with another DB/KB or bodyweight movement.
Squat: If you don’t have a good feel for percentages yet, work to RPE 5-6 for 4 sets of 5 reps across. You should have multiple good reps in the tank on each set.
Dips: If you missed Tuesday’s workout and have the ability, find a heavy 3 weighted strict dip. You could also work on bodyweight, banded, or foot assisted reps.

components.details:
3 Intervals of
3 Min Row for Max Meters
Rest 3 min between Intervals
components.notes:
While simple, this workout will be potent if approached correctly. Focus first and foremost on your technique, not just your effort.
Aim to work at what feels like 85% of your aerobic threshold on the first interval. Another way to guide yourself is by picking a pace you think you could actually hold for closer to 5-6 minutes straight if you needed to.
On interval two, sustain that pace with the goal of achieving a similar meters “score.” On interval three, push a little harder and see if you can squeeze out a bit more!

components.details:
9-15-21 Reps for Time of:
Pull-Ups
Thrusters (95/65#)
components.notes:
This workout is a familiar couplet known as “Fran,” but today we’ll flip it and reverse it! Both the rep sceme and the movement order is reversed.
The intent for today is a quick burn. Fast Fran times are under 4 minutes and today should be under 9! Scale as needed to get a true dose of intensity today.
Pull-Up Scaling:

B. 6-8-10 Strict

5×4 @ 70%-75% / RPE 6-7
components.notes: This is a volume strength session focused on reinforcing front rack position, bracing, and consistent squat mechanics. The load should feel moderate, challenging but never near failure. RPE 6–7 means athletes finish each set with about 3 reps left in the tank.

components.details:

components.notes:
This is accessory work meant to build core strength, stability, and durability, move with control and focus on quality, not speed or max effort.
For the Copenhagen plank, keep your hips high and body in a straight line; the focus is on adductor (inner thigh) strength, so pick a knee or foot position you can hold with good form.
During crossovers, stay light on your feet, find rhythm, and work coordination rather than going all out.
On the medball slams the intention is to focus on rotational core strength, so make sure you are bracing before slamming the ball to the floor.
Finally, in the arch hold, squeeze glutes, keep arms and legs off the ground, and focus on holding a strong, tight shape. Treat this as practice, consistent, high-quality movement and it will pay off in bigger lifts and gymnastics skills later on.

components.notes:
Intent: 2-3 rounds.
This is a long, steady grind with a focus on strict pulling strength and midline endurance. The intent is 2–3 full rounds in 30 minutes, so pace accordingly. Smooth on the machines, steady on the gymnastics.
On the row/bike, think moderate effort, not sprint. Each machine segment should leave you breathing but ready to go straight into the pull-ups.
For the strict chin-ups, break early to avoid failure; small sets with short rests will keep you moving better than big sets to burnout. Scale by using band or foot/box-assistance that provides challenge while allowing for full range of motion on each rep.
On the tuck-ups, stay controlled and keep your lower back pressed to the floor at the bottom of the rep.
Because you switch machines each round, approach this like an endurance piece, find a rhythm you can maintain the whole 30 minutes. Consistency and smart pacing are the keys to hitting the stimulus.

components.notes:
Take 3-4 warm-up sets to find a moderately heavy load (RPE 7-7.5) for 5 reps on the deadlift, then complete 4 work sets across. You should have 2-3 reps in reserve at this weight.
Once at work weight, superset the deadlifts with the pallof press. Maintain a stable position with the back knee hovering just a few inches off the floor as you extend the arms and bring them back into the body.

components.notes:
If you’ve got a buddy in class that runs around your same pace, see if you can inspire a bit of friendly competition today to light a fire and keep you focused. Start your first interval around RPE 8 — vigorous effort, but with a bit left in the tank. Then, challenge each other to see if you can hold pace or get a little bit faster on the next two runs.
Scale to a run distance you can complete in under 3:30.

components.details:

5 sets x 3 reps @ 70%-75% or RPE 6-7
components.notes:
If you have a recent or well-established 1 rep max push jerk, use ~70-75% of that for your work sets. If not, work at about RPE 6-7 for how you feel today. We’re aiming for crisp reps: powerful leg drive, clear timing, accurate footwork, and no press-outs!
We worked a lot on the jerk rack position, dip, and leg drive in the past two weeks. Do your best to incorporate what you practiced into this more dynamic movement.
If you struggle with wrist pain or other discomfort on these lifts, make sure you’re properly re-racking the bar from overhead and getting back to your best possible position each time with the shoulders and trunk supporting the bar, not your hands and arms.

For the lunges, a front rack or back rack hold may be used.
After the lunges, any method of getting the barbell back overhead is allowed (push press, push jerk, split jerk). Hold with straight arms and strong midline stabilization for 15-20 seconds.

components.notes:
Today we celebrate CFSBK’s 18th Anniversary… 18 years of fitness, fun, and foolishness 🤪
This workout is about steady pacing and managing fatigue across multiple movement patterns. Eighteen minutes is long enough that you should avoid redlining early. Aim to finish at least 2 rounds of work, scaling accordingly.
Push-Ups: break them up early if needed to keep form tight. Scale volume or to elevated reps.

Remember why you love this place, cheer on your fellow athletes, and have fun!

Intent <12 min
Snatch: Choose a light load you can complete in 1-3 sets each time. The hang position can be anywhere above the knee today. Always stand up fully to complete the rep before bringing the bar back down to the hang.
Since we are working with light loads, do not bail the bar from overhead today! It destroys the 10 and 15# plates. Control the bar to your hip and then set it down. If you want to bail at the 75lb load, use a 15lb bar + 25lb plates and 5’s on the outside.
Run: Go a little faster than you want to! Scale back to 270m if the full effort will take longer than 2:30.

components.notes: At 75% to 80%, or around RPE 7 to 8, we’re now at moderate-to-heavy load. The weight should feel challenging but not like a true max. Focus on keeping your elbows high, chest tall, and core braced throughout every rep. Each set should feel heavy but repeatable, leaving one to two reps in the tank.

components.details:
“The Predator”
800m Run
200′ Crawl
4 Sandbag Cleans
400m Run
160′ Crawl
8 Sandbag Cleans
200m Run
120′ Crawl
12 Sandbag Cleans
components.notes:
Intent 15-20 min.
Workout courtesy of Coach Cara! A little note from her: “The Predator is a workout model inspired by wolves and other distance predators who have to track and follow their prey for long distances, get close enough to strike, tussle with their prey, then repeat the cycle until they’re able to finish the kill.”
This workout is about grit. The runs get shorter each round, but the crawls and sandbag cleans will feel longer and heavier, so it is important to be stubborn towards the end.
Run: Settle into a controlled pace that allows you to attack the crawl without redlining.
Crawl: Move steadily, and avoid rushing to save your shoulders and core.
Sandbag Cleans: Choose a heavy bag! Brace your core, use your hips; and drive through the floor. Break them into quick singles if needed, but stay close to the bag and reset right away.

components.details:
3-4 Rounds For Quality
1:00 Handstand Hold
12-15 Seated Reverse Flies
:30 Sec Hanging L-Sit Hold
1:00 Crossover Single Unders
components.notes:
This accessory work is designed to build stability, shoulder health, and midline strength while sneaking in some light aerobic movement. The intent is three to four steady rounds where you prioritize strong positions and controlled effort so you finish feeling stronger, not burned out.
HS Hold: Focus on pressing tall through the shoulders, keeping your core tight, and maintaining a hollow body position. Accumulate 1:00 per round, taking breaks as needed. Scale to angled wall-facing hollow inversion hold or box pike hold.
Reverse Flies: Should be done with light weights, moving slowly and squeezing the shoulder blades together on every rep to strengthen the upper back.
L-sit hold: Keep your legs as straight as possible, press down firmly through your arms, and brace your core to hold a tight position for the full thirty seconds with the toes above the hips. Scale by bending one knee or both knees into the chest for a tuck variation. Accumulate time if needed.
Crossover single unders: Play with the skill! Use this as a chance to keep moving while staying relaxed.

components.notes:
This looks simple, but it will be humbling for many of us!
Scale the workout so you can complete your first few rounds in under 35 seconds or so. This will likely stretch out as the workout continues. Be prepared to break your push-ups up and “chip away” with small sets. Keep the integrity of your movement. Hold the standard and complete 150 reps where your chest touches the ground!
Scaling
A. 5 Burpees + 5-7 Push-Ups
B. 3 Burpees + 10 Incline Push-Ups

components.notes:
After 2-3 warm up sets on the barbell, perform the two movements as a superset, resting about a minute between each.
RDL: This is the same rep/tempo scheme as Week 1. Aim to go a bit heavier. Use a regular grip or hook grip for as long as possible.
Step Up: Choose a box that puts your thigh relatively parallel to the floor, rather than a higher box and “below parallel” depth. Challenge yourself on the loading at this mid-range. Minimize push off from the bottom leg as much as possible. Complete all the reps on one side before changing to the other side. You may keep your foot on the box throughout the set or take it off and step it back up, athlete’s choice.

components.details:
5 Intervals of
In 1:30
6 Horizontal Ring Rows
12 Box Jumps (24/20″)
Max Calorie Bike
Rest 1:30
components.notes:
Intent is to have at least 30 seconds on the bike each round. Scale one or both of the first movements as needed to achieve that consistently.
Ring Rows: RX’d version is feet on bench with body completely parallel to floor in start position. Maintain solid plank position throughout and resist the urge to kip the movement or use momentum as fatigue accumulates. Scale by placing feet on the floor and choosing a very difficult angle for 6 unbroken reps, possibly breaking into two quick sets in later rounds.
Box Jump: Scale height of the box as needed to jump today. Fully extend the legs and hips at the top of each rep. Work on cycling reps efficiently: pause briefly at the top to get balanced and stable. Step one foot down, and as the second foot touches the floor jump immediately back to the box. The place to rest or re-group is at the top of the box, not the floor.

components.details:
Push Jerk
5 sets x 2 reps @ 75-80% or RPE 7-8
components.notes:
If you have a recent or well-established 1 rep max push jerk, use ~75-80% of that for your work sets. If not, work at about RPE 7-8 for how you feel today. We’re aiming for crisp reps: powerful leg drive, clear timing, accurate footwork, and no press-outs!
On that note: Locking out a lift requires you establish the overhead position forcefully before the full weight of the bar is pushing down on you. It has to be proactive as part of a continuous, committed motion—you can’t wait to feel the weight and then react to it. Make it a focus on every lift to never let up on pushing up against the bar, and to lock in your shoulder blades forcefully for a solid base to prevent bouncing. Reach and punch up!

Candlestick toe touches: Engage your core and avoid using momentum.
Paused Wall Ball Shots: Hold at the bottom for 1 full second on tension, stay tall, then drive up with power. Up for a challenge? Grab a heavier medicine ball today and get out of your comfort zone!

components.details:

A. 6 Shuttle Runs (40′)

components.notes:
With 8 rounds of work and no rest minute, many athletes will need to scale this workout to make the output sustainable. Remove ego and set yourself up for success today.
The main training goal here is to work efficient kipping pull-up technique. If you’re building mechanics and consistency with this, break your reps in to smart sets right away. If you start to lose range of motion or form degrades, reduce volume of reps per minute. If you are already technically proficient, push for bigger unbroken sets.
Your first two rounds should be a manageable amount of work to complete in ~40 seconds per minute. As you fatigue, effort will need to increase and that time may stretch a bit.
Shuttle Run: Each rep is “down and back” across the tape lines, 40 feet. Complete 6 “down and backs” for a total of 240 feet. If you prefer, just count each time you turn around and count to 12! Touch both feet and 1 hand down on the far side of the line on each turnaround.

RX+ 4-6 Bar Muscle Ups or 8-12 Chest-to-bar Pull-Ups
A. 8-12 Kipping
B. 4-6 Strict (bodyweight)

components.notes:
This workout is short, heavy, and explosive. Every set should feel like a sprint.
Deadlifts: Heavy enough to demand respect, but should still allow for quick singles or small touch-and-go sets. Maintain a flat back and tight brace every rep.

Regardless of your experience level, work at loads that allow you to build confidence through repetition. We’re aiming for crisp reps: powerful leg drive, clear timing, accurate footwork, and no press-outs! We will increase loading over the following three weeks.

Intent is < 6:00. This one is quick and dirty, and provides a perfect opportunity to push yourself. Scale as needed to achieve a high intensity effort from start to finish!
Scale A
12-10-8 Calorie Row
8-10-12 Burpees over the Rower
Scale B
12-10-8 Calorie Row
8-10-12 Burpees

components.details:
Front Squat
4×3 @ 85% – 88% / RPE 8-9
components.notes:
We have heavy triples today. Focus on bracing, maintaining tension at the bottom of the lift, and creating bar speed. Every rep should have a controlled and deliberate descent. Take time between reps at the top to reset; don’t rush.
Expect the weight to feel heavy but doable; leave just about 1 rep in the tank.
Rest 3 minutes or more between sets to recover fully.

components.details:

130m Run
15 Overhead Squats (135/95/65#)
15 Chest to Bar Pull-Ups
270m Run
12 Overhead Squats
12 Chest to Bar Pull-Ups
400m Run
9 Overhead Squats
9 Chest to Bar Pull-Ups
components.notes:
Intent ~8-12 min
Run Scaling: 130m>200>270m
OHS: Moderately heavy load that challenges your stability under fatigue. Reduce load as much as needed to achieve your best mechanics and range of motion today. An empty training bar will still provide a potent workout if the correct intent is applied!
Athletes may complete a full snatch that passes through a below-parallel squat as their first rep or use any method of power snatch to get the barbell overhead and then continue into their set.
CTB: For each rep to count, the athlete’s chest somewhere below the collarbone makes contact with the bar.
A. 12-9-6 CTB Kipping
B. 15-12-9 Chin Over Bar Kipping
C. 8-6-4 Strict Variation (CTB, chin over bar, foot assisted)

components.details:
4 Intervals of:
In 3:00:
Bench Press x 15 Reps
AMRAP Row for Meters
Rest 3:00
components.notes:
This is a repeat! Refer back to 11/16/2024.
This workout is 4 intervals of 3:00 on, 3:00 off with your score being weight used and total meters rowed.
Push hard on the row, but pace strategically so you don’t crash early.
Use the full 3:00 rest to recover; each interval should be treated like a fresh effort.
Bench Press: Try to use the same weight for all 4 sets on the bench press. Choose a weight that you can complete each round in 1–3 sets, about 65–70% of max. Loading at body weight or 3/4 bodyweight would be a lovely challenge for those capable.

components.details:
A1. 4×6 Barbell Good mornings
A2. 4x6ea DB Reverse Lunges
components.notes:
Today’s focus is posterior chain and single-leg strength. After a warm up set or two on the barbell, complete 4 sets of each as a superset. Rest about 60-90 seconds between A1 and A2, and about 1:30-2:00 between full rounds.
Good Mornings: Aim to go heavier than week 2, but only if you can keep a rigid, braced trunk, extended back, and controlled hip hinge.
DB Reverse Lunges: Suitcase style. Go heavier than week 1. Keep balance and smooth control through full range of motion, with the back knee touching the floor lightly on each rep.

components.details:
6 Rounds For Time
12 KB Swings (70/53#)
12 Box Jump Overs
components.notes:
This is a short, powerful workout! Push the pace but keep form sharp and make sure you’re organized for each box jump.
KB Swings: Aim for unbroken sets of 12 with a heavy bell. Drive through the hips, keep shoulders back, and let the bell float.
BJO: Two foot take off, then athletes must step down to the other side of the box. You may face one side of the box or position yourself horizontally to it, and you must travel over to the opposite side. Scale by reducing height of the box. Modify if needed by stepping up to and over the box with both feet.
Move steadily, minimize rest, and keep transitions quick.

components.details:
Split Jerk
4 sets x 2-3 reps @ 75-80%
components.notes:
Today’s focus is on speed, accuracy, and confidence in the split jerk!
At 75–80%, the load should feel challenging but give you room to practice good mechanics.
Prioritize a smooth and controlled dip and fast drive, then punch yourself under the bar with strong, locked-out arms.
Hold your split stance for a moment before recovering, front foot back halfway, then back foot forward to meet it.
Every rep should look the same. Think about building consistency under load, not testing max strength.

components.details:
18 Min for Quality
1:00 Bike for Calories @ RPE 5-6
80′ ea arm Single Arm Farmer Carry
130m Run @ RPE 5-6
80′ ea arm Single Arm Overhead Carry
components.notes:
While this is assistance work, aim for minimal rest and try to just keep moving at a steady groove for the full time.
Bike and run at moderate efforts; you should be able to answer a question but not hold an entire long-winded conversation 😉 Set a baseline for calories in the first round and then aim to hit about that same number in your minute each time.
Choose moderate to heavy loading for the carries, as your mobility and stability allow. In the overhead position, reach through your shoulder and keep the elbow locked out the entire time.

components.details:
A. Front Squat 4×3 @ 85% – 88% / RPE 8-9
B. Bench Press 4 sets x 10-15 reps
C. Deadlift, 4×5 @ RPE 7-7.5
D. Split Jerk, 4 sets x 2-3 reps @ 75-80% / RPE 7-8
components.notes:
Tomorrow we have rowing, double unders and burpees.
You may superset your main lift with another DB/KB or bodyweight movement.
Deadlift: This is the same rep scheme as week 3 if you came to that class try to work a little bit heavier than that day.
Split Jerk: If you are new to this lift, keep a moderate load that allows you to focus on a solid footwork and speed. Mechanics first, then consistency then intensity!

components.details:
AMRAP 8 MIN
4 Strict Chin Ups
8 Goblet Squats (32/24kg)
12 AbMat Sit-Ups
components.notes:
Intent 4+ Rounds
Short and simple burner, aim for steady, unbroken rounds throughout the 8 minutes.
Chin ups: Strict and controlled; break early if needed to avoid hitting failure. Scale volume so you can complete the reps in under 30 sec per round or scale to foot-assisted reps.
Goblet squats: Should feel strong and smooth, keep the chest tall and heels down.
ABmat sit ups: Move fast through these ones but keep tension in the midline to protect your lower back.
The goal is constant movement, find a pace that lets you keep working without long breaks.

components.details:
For Time:
Row 200 Calories
*After every 10 calories, one partner will perform 20 Double Unders and the other will perform 10 Burpees
components.notes:
Intent: 24-30 minutes
One person rows at a time, with the following sequence:
A Rows 10 Calories (B is resting), then
*A performs 20 Double Unders, B performs 10 Burpees
B Rows 10 Calories (A is resting), then
*B performs 20 Double Unders, A performs 10 Burpees
Continue alternating with this format until a total of 200 calories have been rowed as a team!
Ideally, each partner will end up completing 100 calories on the erg, 200 double unders, and 100 burpees.
Stay sharp on transitions, quick switches keep the pace high and prevent wasted time.
This workout is more about steady grind than sprinting; pace your burpees and double unders so you can maintain rhythm all the way through.
Scaling
Burpees: Reduce to 7–8 reps or no push up burpees.
Double Unders: 40 single unders or :20/:30 sec of DU’S attempts.
Row: Reduce total to 150 calories for newer athletes.

components.details:
A. Front Squat 4×3 @ 85% – 88% / RPE 8-9
B. Bench Press 4 sets x 10-15 reps
C. Deadlift, 4×5 @ RPE 7-7.5
D. Split Jerk, 4 sets x 2-3 reps @ 75-80% / RPE 7-8
components.notes:
Tomorrow we have front squats, power cleans, and running.
You may superset your main lift with another DB/KB or bodyweight movement.
Deadlift: This is the same rep scheme as week 3. If you came to that class try to work a little bit heavier than that day.
Split Jerk: If you are new to this lift, keep a moderate load that allows you to focus on a solid footwork and speed. Mechanics first, then consistency then intensity!

components.details:
20 Rounds for Time
10 Ball Slams
100′ Sled Sprint
components.notes:
In teams of four athletes, with one person working at a time, take turns on full rounds of the couplet until the team has finished 20 rounds, 5 for each person.
Use light weights today. Almost all athletes will get the most effective workout today by using an empty sled. Practice cycling your ball slams efficiently and then… sprint!

components.details:
Front Squat
4×2 @ 88% – 90% / RPE 8-9
components.notes:
Heavy doubles today.
Every rep should be controlled, tight, and explosive out of the hole.
Expect the bar to feel challenging and slower than previous weeks, but form must stay sharp. Leave about 1 rep in the tank.
Rest ~3 minutes between sets to recover fully and keep quality high.

components.details:
3 Rounds for Time:
550m Run
7 Power Cleans 185/135#
Intent <15 min
components.notes:
This workout is meant to be a gritty, medium length effort with a balance of running and heavy barbell work.
The 550m run should feel like ~2:30–3:00 of work at a steady but pushable pace. Use it as controlled effort, not a jog.
The 7 power cleans should be heavy enough that you need to break into singles or small sets. Move efficiently, set up well each rep, keep the bar close, and receive in a strong, stable position.
Aim for consistent round times and avoid blowing up early.
Scaling
Weight: 155/135/115/95/65 Reduce load to allow steady singles with good form and/or cap barbell reps at 5.
Run: 400m/270m

components.details: Bar Muscle Up
components.notes:
Spend time dialing in the swing and timing, strong, controlled kip with active lats and tight body line.
Don’t rush the turnover; wait until you feel your hips rise before pulling the bar down and behind you.
Keep your arms straight longer and use your hips to create lift, not just your arms.
Some helpful cues:
“Push down on the bar, not away.”
“Hips to bar, then pull through.”
Scaling
Work on kip swings, chest-to-bar pull-ups, jumping bar muscle-ups, or transition drills using a low bar setup or band.

components.details:
4 Rounds, Each for Time
15/12 Bike Calories
5 Bar Muscle-ups
*Complete 1 round every 4 minutes. Go as fast as possible on each round.
components.notes:
Straightforward intervals today, so choose a gymnastic scale that challenges your skill and strength. You should aim to work hard for all 4 rounds and choose a variation that allows you to be successful, rather than hit a wall of failing multiple reps or sacrificing range of motion.
Bike < 90 sec. Scale back as needed.
BMU Scaling
A. 2-4 reps
B. 10 CTB Pull-Ups + 10 Strict Dips (matador/ring)
C. 10 Kipping Pull-Ups + 10 Box Dips
D. 5 Strict Pull-Ups (bw or assisted) + 10 Box Dips

components.details:
A1. 4×6 Barbell Romanian Deadlifts @ 3111
A2. 4x6ea DB Bulgarian Split Squats
components.notes:
Posterior chain strength and balance! Move with control and tension. After 2-3 warm up sets on the barbell, perform the two movements as a superset, resting about 60-90 sec between each. You should leave a little in the tank (RPE 7–8). Each set should feel challenging but not grindy.
RDLs: Aim to go heavier than Weeks 1 and 4. Hinge at the hips with a flat back, soft knees, and full hamstring stretch each rep. If you’re very mobile and stable, try adding a deficit by standing on a plate for extra range.
Bulgarian split squats: Should be steady and balanced, keep your chest tall, front foot flat, and knee tracking over toes.
Tempo and control are key! Think strength through tension, not speed.

components.details:
18 min for Quality:
1:00 Sandbag Carry
30-45 sec each Stagger Stance Wall Sit Hold
1:00 Bike/Row/Jog
20 Tuck Ups
components.notes:
This is a 18-minute quality-focused piece, aim for steady effort and control rather than intensity.
Sandbag Carry: Stay tall, brace your core, and keep steady breathing, switch positions if needed (bear hug, shoulder).
Stagger stance wall sit: Should challenge your quads. Keep your back flat to the wall.
Bike/row/jog: Active recovery. Keep it light and rhythmic to bring your heart rate down.
Tuck Ups: Tight core, controlled reps, and focus on hollow body tension.
Scaling
Wall Sit: Two legs
Tuck ups: For folks struggling to coordinate upper/lower body timing and reseting to a strong hollow body shape after each rep, do knee tucks!

components.details:
Split Jerk
4 sets x 2 reps @ 80%-85%+
components.notes:
Today’s goal is still speed, accuracy, and confidence under the bar, not maximal load. The weight should feel challenging but allow for crisp, consistent reps. Every rep should look the same!
Focus on an upright dip, explosive drive, and fast punch under the bar. Land in a stable split stance, front foot flat, front shin vertical, back heel lifted, knees bent, and bar stacked directly over the shoulders.
Hold your catch position for a brief pause before recovering, front foot back, then back foot forward.

components.details:
3 Rounds for Total Reps
1:00 Wall Walks
1:00 Shuttle Run (40 ft)
1:00 Alternating DB Snatch (50/35/20#)
1:00 Bike
1:00 Rest
components.notes:
This is a Fight Gone Bad-style workout. Athletes will start at various stations. On a running clock, accumulate reps at each station. There is no extra rest or transition time between stations. Everyone will move through a 4 minute round and rest at the same time on the fifth minute in each round.
This workout is all about steady, sustained effort across movements. Pace early and aim to stay consistent through all 3 rounds to get the most work done in the total time allotted.
Wall walks: Move smoothly and avoid rushing; focus on strong shoulders and controlled descents. Scale range of motion or accumulate time in an angled hollow inversion hold.
Shuttle run: 1 rep = 40 feet = 20 ft down and 20 ft back.
DB snatches: Alternate arms each rep, keep the back flat, and use your hips to drive the dumbbell overhead.
Bike: Find a solid pace you can hold for the minute without redlining.
Use the 1-minute rest to walk around, shake out your arms, and control your breathing before the next round.

components.details:
A. Front Squats 4×2 @ 88% – 90% / RPE 8-9
B. Weighted Chin-ups 3-3-3-3-3
C. Barbell Romanian Deadlifts 4×6 @ 3111 Tempo
D. Split Jerk, 4 sets x 2 reps @ 80%-85%+
components.notes:
Tomorrow we have wall ball, double unders, and toes to bar.
You may superset your main lift with another DB/KB or bodyweight movement.
RDLs: This is the same rep scheme as weeks 1 and 4. If you hit those exposures, try to work a little bit heavier today while maintaining form and tempo.
Split Jerk: If you are new to this lift, keep a moderate load that allows you to focus on a solid footwork and speed. Mechanics first, then consistency then intensity!
Chin-Up Progression: We last saw weighted chin-ups (doubles) in Week 4, so you can track back for guidance today. Do a couple of warm up sets (foot assisted ring pull-ups, negatives, lock offs, etc.). Then choose a difficult variation for you that allows for consistent mechanics and full ranges of motion. Examples:
A. 5 Sets x 3 weighted Chin-Ups, building to find a heavy triple
B. 5-7 Sets x 1-3 bodyweight Chin-Ups or Negatives
C. 5 Sets x 5 tough reps of Box Pike or Foot Assisted Chin-Ups

components.details:
AMRAP 12 MIN
Row for Meters
*Non-rowing partner holds a Forearm Plank. Trade off as desired.
components.notes:
Team effort today! Your meters only count when your partner is holding a solid forearm plank, so communication and timing are key.
Take turns rowing in consistent, powerful intervals (e.g., 250–500m), depending on your capacity and how long your partner can hold the plank.
Row: Stay strong and efficient, big drive with the legs, smooth pull, and controlled recovery.
Plank: Focus on tight glutes, braced core, and steady breathing. Avoid sagging hips or piking up.
The goal is steady output for 12 minutes, not an all-out sprint early. Find a rhythm that keeps both athletes moving and engaged.

components.details:
For Time
60 Wall Ball Shots (20#, 10′ / 14#, 9′)
180 Double Unders
60 Toes to Bar
components.notes:
This is a chipper style workout, where all repetitions of the first movement must be completed before moving to the second, and again to the third.
Create a gameplan today, don’t just go in blind. That being said, staying flexible with the plan will help many of us achieve our best time!
If you’re typically conservative, maybe today is a good opportunity to push for bigger sets. If you often overestimate your capacity and flame out early, perhaps playing with the other end of the spectrum is worth a try.
Either way… work hard and have fun with this one!
Wall Ball: 1-4 sets. Scale med ball weight and target height. further as needed.
Double Unders: Scale to a rep count you can complete in under 5 minutes.
TTB: 3-8 sets. Scale to 40 kipping reps, 30 strict reps, partial range of motion, or 60 sit-ups.

components.details:
A. Front Squats 4×2 @ 88% – 90% / RPE 8-9
B. Weighted Chin-ups 3-3-3-3-3
C. Barbell Romanian Deadlifts 4×6 @ 3111 Tempo
D. Split Jerk, 4 sets x 2 reps @ 80%-85%+
components.notes:

You may superset your main lift with another DB/KB or bodyweight movement.
RDLs: This is the same rep scheme as weeks 1 and 4. If you hit those exposures, try to work a little bit heavier today while maintaining form and tempo.
Split Jerk: If you are new to this lift, keep a moderate load that allows you to focus on a solid footwork and speed. Mechanics first, then consistency then intensity!

Do a couple of warm up sets (foot assisted ring pull-ups, negatives, lock offs, etc.). Then choose a difficult variation for you that allows for consistent mechanics and full ranges of motion. Examples:

components.details:
For Time
270m Run, each
400m Run, each
550m Run, each
components.notes:
Buddy up and get a move on! Partner A starts by running 270m, and upon returning to the gym tags in Partner B to do their length.
With about 3/4 mile total distance here, these should be tough efforts right out the gate.
The stronger runner (or whoever is more confident in “recovering” better) should likely go first today, as they’ll have less rest than the second partner going into each subsequently longer interval.
Scale: If your mile pace is over 12 min or you are building your tolerance to running, consider scaling to:
200m / 270m / 400m (Total distance is just over half a mile)

components.details:
Front Squat
5×1 @ 90% – 95% / RPE 8.5-9
components.notes:
Today is a heavy front squat day! Focus on tension, control, and confidence under load.
At 90–95% / RPE 8.5–9, every single should feel heavy but technically solid. Take time to brace properly. Big breath, tight core, elbows high, and chest tall. Keep your midline engaged throughout the rep, especially in the turnover, and drive straight up out of the hole.
Treat each single as practice for your next PR: perfect setup, perfect execution!
Rest 2–3 minutes between sets to recover and maintain quality.

components.details:
AMRAP 8:00
5-10-15-20-25-30…etc.
KB Swings (24/16kg)
Push Ups
components.notes:
This short AMRAP is a grip and upper-body endurance burner. Pace early and stay smooth.
The rep scheme climbs fast, so don’t sprint the early rounds; find a rhythm you can sustain. The goal is steady movement for the full 8 minutes; avoid long rests once fatigue sets in.
For KB swings, keep the hinge sharp, drive with your hips, not your arms. Stay tall and breathe at the top.
Push-ups will add up quickly! Maintain tight midline, full range of motion, and break before hitting failure.
PU Scale:
A. Volume (ex: 3-6-9-12-etc.)
B. Incline Push-up — choose a height you can complete about 8-12 unbroken reps at when fresh!

components.details: Rope Climbs
components.notes: Your coach will take you through a short progression to work on the footwork and foundations of this skill. Beginner athletes can expect to get an understanding of mechanics needed and elements to work on. More experienced athletes should come ready to learn how to make their existing skills more efficient!

components.details:
20 Minutes for Quality
1-3 Rope Climbs (15′)
30 sec each: DB Side Plank
400m Run
components.notes:
The intent for today is sustainable, quality effort. Choose a rope climb scale that allows you to practice the skill while working safely under moderate fatigue. If you’re advanced, you might see how quickly you can complete 3 reps each time you get back to the rope.
*If you missed yesterday’s workout, option is to sub in 10-20 push-ups per round instead of side planks!
A. 1 Partial Height Climb
B. 3-5 Rig Pull-Up with Rope Footwork
C. 2-3 Supine-to-Stand-to-Supine Climbs

components.details:
2 Sets
10-15+ DB Supinated Bicep Curls
10-15 Banded Reverse Flyes
components.notes:
Curls: Pick a weight you cannot complete more than 20 reps with when fresh. On your second set through, go to failure. Resist the urge to use momentum.
Flyes: Keep your ribs stacked over your pelvis (not flared forward) and squeeze/wrap the shoulder-blades together as you pull back.

components.details:
A1. Deadlift, 8-6-4-8
A2. Split Squat Pallof Hold, 4 x 20 sec each
components.notes:
Deadlift: Today’s sets are a “wave.” Begin with 2-4 warm-up sets to find a starting point for your first work set: a moderately heavy 8 reps. Increase the weight for the set of 6 and again for the set of 4 reps.
The final 8 reps will be a “drop set.” You can repeat the same load you used in the first set or ideally go a bit heavier.
SSPH: Hover the back knee just a couple inches off of the floor throughout the hold. Keep ribcage stacked over the pelvis and torso upright.

components.details:
Tabata Mash-Ups!
8 Rounds / 4 Minutes
A. Double Unders
B. Sandbag Bearhug Hold
Rest 2 min
8 Rounds / 4 Minutes
A. Box Jumps (24/20″)
B. Dual KB Suitcase Hold (32/24kg ea)
components.notes:
Tabata is 20 seconds of work / 10 seconds of rest. Alternate movements back and forth (A/B) for 8 total rounds, 4 of each. Rest and use the same structure for the second couplet.
Go for max reps each round on the jumping movements and choose challenging weights for your holds. Grit it out!
Use this format to practice double unders, regardless of skill level.
Land as tall and lightly on the box as possible today. Fully extend the knees and hips before stepping down.

components.details:
EOMOM x 10 Min
2 Split Jerks
components.notes: After a few minutes to warm up, perform a set of 2 jerks every 2:00 for 5 sets. If technique is on point and reps are feeling crisp, aim to go a bit heavier than last week (80-85%). If not or if you’re newer to this variation, stay at a load that allows you to make adjustments and practice good reps to finish out this cycle!

components.details:
For Time:
1000/800m Row
– into –
10 Dual DB Devil’s Press
20 Dual DB Front Rack Lunges
30 Burpees
20 Dual DB Front Rack Lunges
10 Dual DB Devil’s Press
components.notes:
Workout courtesy of Coach Phil!
Time Cap: 15 min
Row < 4 min
DB: 50/35/20# ea hand.
Choose a DB weight that you can maintain proper midline stabilization with and good overhed position at the top of each rep of the devil’s press, as well as complete the lunges in 1-2 sets.
This is a challenging movement to organize, especially under fatigue. Remove ego and scale as needed!

components.details:
18 Min for Quality
16 Alternating Tall Kneeling Rotational Ball Slams
30 sec each Single Leg Hamstring Bridge Hold
1:00 Bike/Row/Jog/Jump Rope
30 sec L-Sit
components.notes:
Today is about control, position, and quality movement, not intensity or speed. Move with purpose and stay focused on good mechanics!
Ball Slams: Rotate through the torso, stay tall, and use your hips/core to generate power rather than just throwing with the arms.
Single-leg hamstring hold: Drive your heel down, keep your hips level, and focus on feeling the hamstring load, not your lower back!
Cardio: Should be smooth, conversational, and used as active recovery before the core work.
L-sit: Stay tight and fight for a strong position; break once or twice if needed, but maintain quality throughout. Scale to a tuck hold or floor pike hold.

components.details:
A. Front Squats 5X1 @ 90% – 95% / RPE 8.5-9
B. Deadlift 8-6-4-8
C. Split Jerk 5×2, building
D. Tempo Matador Dips, 4 x 6-8 @ 30×1
components.notes:
Tomorrow we have air squats, power cleans, strict pull-ups, and running.
You may superset your main lift with another DB/KB or bodyweight movement.
Front Squat: Heavy singles mean strong bracing, tall chest, and confidence out of the bottom.
Deadlifts: The 8-6-4-8 wave should build, then back off. Keep your back tight and hinge clean.
Split Jerk: If you are new to this lift, keep a moderate load that allows you to focus on a solid footwork and speed. Mechanics first, then consistency then intensity!
Matador Dips: Time under tension, stay strict, feel the tempo; and build control in the pressing muscles.

components.details:
6 Rounds for Time
30 Air Squats
19 Power Cleans (135/95#)
7 Strict Pull-ups
400m Run
components.notes:
Today is the final Saturday of our 8-week cycle, and we’re closing it out with purpose. “Hotshots 19” is a tribute workout honoring the 19 members of the Granite Mountain Hotshots firefighting team who tragically lost their lives while fighting a fire in Yarnell, Arizona.
Approach this piece with respect, grit, and intention. This is a long workout, so settle into a steady rhythm.
Air Squat: Move with quality and keep the integrity of the range of motion!
Power Cleans: Stay disciplined with controlled singles or small sets.
Strict pull-ups: Break early if you need to, to keep form sharp.
Run: Use it to breathe, reset, and stay mentally locked in, preparing to come back in and work with focus, toughness, and consistency, round after round.
You’ve built strength and capacity these past 8 weeks and the whole year! Today is where it shows.
Scaling
This Hero WOD is long and high volume. Reduce the reps and load to keep this workout under 40 minutes.
Power Clean: 135/115/95/75/55
Pull-Ups: Strict, Assisted, Kipping, Ring Rows
Run: Suggest keeping the full volume run today OR complete 200m run + 400m bike per round
Newer or deconditioned athletes might also consider scaling their version of the workout to 4 rounds instead of 6 so there is less overall volume of work today.

components.details:
A. Front Squats 5X1 @ 90% – 95% / RPE 8.5-9
B. Deadlift 8-6-4-8
C. Split Jerk 5×2, building
D. Tempo Matador Dips, 4 x 6-8 @ 30×1
Front Squat: Heavy singles mean strong bracing, tall chest, and confidence out of the bottom.
Deadlifts: The 8-6-4-8 wave should build, then back off. Keep your back tight and hinge clean.
Split Jerk: If you are new to this lift, keep a moderate load that allows you to focus on a solid footwork and speed. Mechanics first, then consistency then intensity!
Matador Dips: Time under tension, stay strict, feel the tempo; and build control in the pressing muscles.

AMRAP 15 Min
20 Sit-Ups
12/9 Calorie Bike
components.notes:
Partners alternate full rounds. Partner A completes 20 sit-ups + 12/9 bike, then Partner B does the same.
Score = total rounds.
Sustainable, aerobic pacing. Rounds should take ~1:10–1:40, depending on bike power. Goal is to maintain relatively consistent round times across all 15 minutes, not fade in the back half.
Sit-ups: Smooth and unbroken. Use them to breathe before the bike.
Bike: < 45 sec at a strong effort, controlled push. Beware of going all-out, especially in the initial rounds.
Focus on quick transitions on and off the bike. Communicate with your partner, call out when you’re a few cals from done so they can get ready.

components.details:
A: Pull-Ups
4×5-8 reps
B: DB Curls
3×10-15 reps
components.notes:
Pull-ups: Perform 3–4 warm-up sets with ring rows, scap pulls, and light assisted pull-ups, then complete 4 sets of 5-8 reps. Choose the hardest variation you can perform with full range of motion — bodyweight, weighted, or self-assisted. Cluster sets (e.g., 3 reps + 2 reps) are allowed if you can’t perform 5-8 unbroken BW reps but have strict pull-ups. Leave 0–1 reps in reserve.
Curls: perform 1 quick warm-up set followed by two sets in the 10-15 range which should both go to or near failure.

components.details:
AMRAP 12:00
12 Calorie Row or 9 Calorie Bike

“Grace” is one of CrossFit’s classic benchmarks — fast, heavy, and simple. The intent is an all-out sprint while maintaining crisp movement quality.

This interval piece uses a very high work-to-rest ratio (1:7+), which allows for true sprint effort on every :20 interval. Because of the long recovery, the :20 sprints primarily train the phosphagen (ATP–CP) energy system — the system responsible for maximal power output in short bursts of 10–20 seconds. Here’s how you should approach each round:
– Ramp Up: Make this uncomfortable but something you could sustain for a minute at most.
– :20–:30 hard effort: something that feels closer to a :30-:40 max effort
– Sprints: All out effort, its only :20 and you’ll get full recovery. Drop the hammer.

components.details: Rope Climbs
components.notes:
Friendly PSA: Learning how to efficiently climb a rope can be brutal for the skin on your legs before you get the technique down. We recommend wearing long pants and/or a pair of tall socks or even knee sleeves around your ankles.
Use today’s time to learn and practice technique. This video link is set at a point to show a close up of a very efficient footwork method, as well as a reminder that nailing secure footwork will mean you can use your arms less and do more work in less time (increased work capacity = fitness!)
More experienced athletes can work on completing a 15′ climb in as few “pulls” as possible. For example: 3-4 “reps” of footwork + pull to get to the top, rather than 5-6 on each climb.

This workout offers 5 max-effort attempts at each exercise, regardless of how you modify the movements. Choose something that will allow you to perform at least 7 reps of each, even as you fatigue.
Give yourself between 3-5 minutes of rest after the pull-ups before beginning the next round of bench presses so you recover enough to get another big set.
All athletes should perform the bench presses with a buddy — spotting this movement is essential under fatigue.
Less-experienced athletes should reduce the load of the barbell and the difficulty of the pull-up:
Bench Press
A. 3/4 bodyweight
B. 1/2 bodyweight
C. Any load that allows for at least 7 tough reps per set
Pull-Up
A. Max reps bodyweight + band or foot assist to get to at least 7 reps per set
B. Band or Foot Assist
C. Ring Row

René Brink Jakobsen of Vang, Denmark, died Jan. 3, 2013, after being hit by an improvised explosive device while on foot patrol with his unit in Upper Gereshk Valley in Helmand Province, Afghanistan. This is a CrossFit mainsite workout from 2/27/24, and we last performed it on 3/6/25 in slightly abbreviated form. Track back in your training log for qualitative and quantitative notes!
Today’s workout is a classic heavy day. Even though most athletes can perform this workout as prescribed, the challenge lies in the technical complexities of the movements. Adding load should be based on your ability to stay mechanically sound.
Each athlete, regardless of experience, should focus on technique before adding load.
There is a tendency among new CrossFit athletes and trainers to avoid heavy days entirely or execute them incorrectly. However, CrossFit is a strength and conditioning program. While people sometimes characterize CrossFit by its programming of mixed-modal workouts for time (“met-cons”), this is a limited view. Days devoted to strength training are essential to CrossFit and are integral to CrossFit’s prescription of constantly varied workouts… continue reading on CrossFit.com here

Volume Modifications
This simply means decreasing the total number of reps or the distance on the run. A common sub would be to do 3/4 of the volume on the calisthenics or 2/3 distance on each of the mile runs. You can decrease volume across the board, or only on the movements that you struggle most with.

Finally, perhaps it’s just the muscular stamina that will catch up to you. For example if Push-Ups are the hardest part of this workout, you can perform 20 rounds of:5 Push-Ups, 5 Pull-Ups, 5 Push-Ups, 15 squats to break up the push-ups into two sets of five.

components.notes:
Work in teams of four athletes. Three athletes will work at the same time, while one is resting.
We have a sprinting effort, followed by a rest, and then two more “active rest” stations with holds before moving back to the sprint.
“A” station is the timekeeper and should move as fast as possible. Athlete A will complete sit-ups and sprint while B rests, C holds KBs, and D holds a sandbag (they are next in line to sprint). When A finishes their round of work, implements can go down and everyone rotates to the next station.
The athlete who performed the couplet (A) will rest, athlete holding the sandbag (D) will now complete the couplet, athlete who started with KBs (C) moves to sandbag, and the resting athlete (B) now picks up the KBs.
The athlete performing the couplet can only begin their work when the next two athletes have picked up their implements!
Continue in this fashion for 5 rounds each athlete, 20 rounds total.
Use an empty sled (~85-115#) to keep a true sprint for every round. Use heavy Sandbags and KBs for the holds. Keep transitions tight to maximize your team’s intensity today!

components.notes:
From Coach Katie!
“This workout I’ve written symbolizes some of my favorite things. I’m known for writing spicy grinder pieces, which felt only appropriate because as we know, pregnancy is a marathon both mentally and physically. I LOVE power cleans, burpees, and strongman everything. The workout structure is dedicated to my due date and the length of time I hope to spend creating this baby, no more no less!!! lol
-9 months: 9 rounds
-8/22 is my due date: 8 devils clean, 22 cal machine
-40 weeks: 40M farmers carry”
Devil’s Clean: 1 DB in each hand. Use a load you can move through 8 reps unbroken for most, if not all, of the workout. To scale, remove the push-up from some or all of your reps.
Machine: Scale for a < 2:00 effort.
Carry: Use one of your DBs, traveling a total distance of 40 meters, trading arms as desired throughout. If you are going lighter on the Cleans and want to carry heavier, use a KB instead.
Timecap: 40 min

components.notes:
Helen is considered to be one of the original staple CrossFit benchmark workouts. It was first programmed on CrossFit.com in August 2003. Helen was the first classic benchmark workout that included running. It was the first benchmark workout that had all three major movement modalities of monostructural, weightlifting, and gymnastics , and it was the first benchmark that is a task-priority triplet.
When this workout was first published, the fastest posted time was 8:25 by Greg Amundson. Currently, the fastest times for this workout are under 7 minutes, and high-level athletes will pace it similarly to running a mile as fast as possible. Striving for successful completion in under 15 minutes is typically a great goal to achieve, regardless of performing the workout as prescribed or scaling it. This workout challenges cardio-respiratory endurance, stamina, pull-up capacity, and grip strength.
“Helena” was introduced as a beefed up version of “Helen” for the 2023 CrossFit Games. Switching the Kettlebell Swing for a snatch (easier to judge) and increasing the gymnastic skill from pull-ups to bar muscle-ups. Jeff Adler finished in 7:56, can you beat him?

Where do you go when the going gets tough? Have a plan for what you’ll do with the feeling that inevitably pops up when you’ve done 10 burpee box jumps and have ::checks notes:: 30 reps left.
Your mind and body are both a part of training. Acknowledge it, work with it, and see what’s possible.
KB: Scale to a load you can do at least 15 reps unbroken.
BBJ: Scale to a height you can complete at least 8 reps per minute at a sustainable, not threshold, pace. Make sure to hit full hip and knee extension at the top of every rep today.

components.notes:
This classic CrossFit Benchmark chipper will push your muscular stamina while being metabolically taxing. Complete all of the pull-ups before moving to the push-ups, and so on.
There are over 85,000 logged results for this workout on Beyond the Whiteboard! See what the community is capable of here.
Try to avoid any one exercise taking more than 8 minutes.

components.notes:
Segmented Snatch Pull: Pause for one full second at three positions: 1″ off the floor, at the knee knee, and mid-thigh. Then complete the snatch pull, driving vertically and finishing tall.
Use moderate loads that provide feedback while allowing for proper position and balance throughout the whole lift. Consider this a “primer” before the full lift.
Snatch: Build across the 6-8 sets, using moderate to heavier loads, as technique allows. These are full/squat snatches.

components.notes:
Track back to Week 4 and aim to go a bit heavier. After 1-2 warm-up sets, perform 4 work sets.

The lunge loading can be progressive or sets across. Either way, aim for at least 2 sets at RPE 8+.
If you’d like to superset with a simple bodyweight movement, feel free!

components.details:
2 Sets:
4:00 Row or Ski
3:00 Recovery
4:00 Bike
3:00 Recovery
components.notes:
Today’s workout is about sustained effort and endurance, rather than a score for max reps. Find a pace you can hold steadily across the interval instead of sprinting the first minute. If you wear a heart rate monitor, aim to spend most of your work periods at 85-90% of your HR Max. In the recovery, try to come down to ~60-70%.
Row Pacing:
Use a split that is ~3–8 seconds slower than your 2,000m average.
We last tested our 2K Row on 6/25/26.
Example A:
2K time is 7:56
Average split = 1:59/500m.
Row at 2:02-2:07 for these intervals.
Example B:
2K time is 8:45
Average split = 2:11/500m.
Row at 2:14-2:19 for these intervals.
If you don’t know your 2K time, start by rowing at a pace you could sustain for 10+ minutes. If you get through the first interval without deviating, increase pace slightly for second set.
Bike:
Start at a pace you could sustain for 10+ minutes. Watch RPMs or Watts. Aim to hold a consistent number for the entire interval. Make adjustments as needed. Repeat for second set.
Recovery Period: Continue moving on the machine for 2 minutes at a lighter effort. In final minute, get up, shake it out, and transition to the next machine.

12-15 ea Single Leg Calf Raise*
components.notes: We have C&J and Toes to Bar tomorrow. If you were here Sat/Mon, do DB rows today.

components.notes:
Use today’s work to set yourself up for success on the Metcon. In the first 2-4 sets, practice cycling the barbell from overhead, maintaining mid-foot balance and regaining your hook grip. On the singles, build to a weight heavier than what you’ll use in the metcon to dial in your aggression, timing, and confidence.
Plan to complete one set about every 2 min.

Barbell: light-moderate load you could cycle a few reps with, but might choose singles in the workout to stay consistent. Using ~60-70% of a 1RM is a decent guideline.
Masters 55+ = 115/65lb
